extracted.intended_audience: college administrators, faculty, and higher-education policymakers interested in faculty grantsmanship and institutional support for grant seeking
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and improving faculty involvement in grant-seeking and grant-writing activities at state colleges by identifying barriers, motivators, and institutional supports. The report surveys faculty participation and offers recommendations institutions can use to foster grantsmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of faculty engagement in sponsored research
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of how many faculty are actively engaged in sponsored research or grant-development activities (study found less than 20% were actively engaged; nearly half reported they rarely or never engaged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participation rates to assess current campus culture around grants; low engagement signals need for institutional interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Released time from teaching and advising
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty generally desired released time from teaching and advising to concentrate on sponsored research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide course-release or reduced advising loads as a tangible incentive and enabling resource for faculty to pursue grant work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy teaching loads as an obstacle
rubrics_metrics.description: Heavy teaching loads were identified as an obstacle that prevented faculty from participating in sponsored research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and mitigate teaching load burdens (e.g., redistributed courses, adjunct support) to remove a primary participation barrier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other scholarly and entrepreneurial interests as competing priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty cited other scholarly and entrepreneurial interests that compete with time for grant development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize competing professional commitments when designing incentives; align grant opportunities with faculty interests where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee work as an obstacle
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee work was reported as an obstacle preventing participation in grant-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit or reprioritize service expectations for faculty pursuing grant activity; provide administrative coverage when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of advance warning about opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of advance warning about grant opportunities was cited as a barrier to faculty participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve communication and early notice of funding opportunities so faculty can plan and allocate time to prepare proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of extra clerical/administrative help
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty who engaged in grant-related activities more often reaped benefits of extra clerical help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide administrative/clerical support (budget prep, submission logistics) as an institutional facilitator for grant seeking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition for grant work in college publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition for grant-related work (e.g., in college publications) was associated with faculty engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public recognition and internal publicity as motivational incentives to encourage faculty involvement in grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to technical assistance for grant development
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty who engaged in grant activities were more likely to seek and receive technical assistance in other areas; technical assistance was emphasized as important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer workshops, proposal development help, grant-writing support, and one-on-one technical assistance to increase successful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Junior faculty access to technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Junior faculty reported that they received technical assistance less frequently than their senior colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target outreach and support services to junior faculty (mentoring, tailored assistance) to address disparities and build capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-linked emphasis on assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Data indicated no overall difference between male and female professors except that females were more likely to stress the importance of technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider gendered preferences and needs when designing support programs; ensure equitable access and communication of assistance resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional recommendations to foster grantsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The study concludes with specific recommendations for institutions to foster grantsmanship among faculty (implied supports include released time, clerical help, recognition, and technical assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a package of institutional policies—time release, administrative support, recognition, and proactive technical assistance—to increase faculty engagement in grant seeking.
